outline.title: Code for Resilience
outline.summary: Title slide: Balangiga LGU disaster-response platform; architecture, offline-first communications, and command-center operations.
outline.image_plan: /home/ubuntu/upload/search_images/voCloeqroKQe.png - Map showing the location of Balangiga in Eastern Samar, providing geographical context for the disaster-response platform.

outline.title: The operating reality is fragmented during a crisis
outline.summary: Frame the Balangiga disaster context and the need for a resilient local response loop that works through signal and power disruptions.

outline.title: One system connects warning, movement, and assistance
outline.summary: Show how residents, municipal operations, resilient transport, and visible data freshness connect into one response loop.

outline.title: A layered architecture keeps critical actions local
outline.summary: Present the React Native, FastAPI, PostGIS, transport, and Next.js layers as a cohesive municipal system.

outline.title: Offline SOS turns a weak signal into an actionable record
outline.summary: Explain minimum SOS capture, compact signed SMS payloads, durable outbox storage, and dispatcher visibility of delivery channel.

outline.title: Spatial intelligence routes people away from active flood zones
outline.summary: Explain PostGIS hazard polygons, evacuation center points, flood-intersection filtering, and safe-route output.

outline.title: The LGU dashboard turns incoming signals into a triage queue
outline.summary: Feature the implemented command-center dashboard, including metrics, risk layers, SOS queue, triage drawer, and verified alert feed.

outline.title: The response loop is designed for the first critical minutes
outline.summary: Summarize the operational cycle of verify, locate, route, dispatch, and reconcile.

outline.title: The current build is a runnable foundation
outline.summary: Summarize implemented backend, dashboard, mobile prototype, verification results, and seeded demo baseline.

outline.title: From prototype to operational readiness
outline.summary: Close with the required GIS, security, messaging, observability, and field-exercise work before operational use.
